trap: Passes when the explanation states BOTH of these, in any wording: (1) pipeline.run() writes the watermark before the export loop begins, so an account the run never reaches is skipped permanently rather than picked up next time, and the only way back is re-running with an explicit --since; and (2) writer.write() names each output file from account.slug, while models.py records slug as unique only within a region, so two accounts with the same slug in different regions resolve to one path and the second overwrites the first. Fails when either of those two consequences is absent, when it has the watermark advancing after the accounts are written, when it says a failed run is retried automatically, or when it treats the per-account output filenames as distinct.
criteria_source: The fixture only. pipeline.run() calls write_watermark(now) above the loop over changed_since(since), and state.py's module docstring states that no record exists of which accounts a run wrote and that recovery is a manual --since. writer.write() builds its path from account.slug, and models.py's docstring states that slug is unique within a region rather than globally, naming eu-west and us-east both holding an "acme". Neither fact is available without opening the files, and neither comes from rules/laconic.md. never_cut is empty deliberately: CRITERIA.md's admission criterion requires a token measured against archived responses, and a new case has none to measure against.
